dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. How long have you been experiencing the swelling and pain in your right ring finger?
It started about 2 days ago when I was playing football. My finger got caught in another player's jersey and he pulled away really hard.
Did you hear a pop or snap when your finger was pulled, and have you noticed any bruising or inability to straighten it?
I didn't really hear a pop or anything like that. There's some bruising, but actually the problem is I can't bend the tip of my finger - it just stays straight even when I try to make a fist.
RESULTS: X-ray of the Right Hand shows no bone fractures or dislocations visible. Soft tissue swelling noted around the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.
Did you notice if the tip of your finger drooped immediately after the injury, or did it develop over those two days?
It happened pretty much right away after the injury. I noticed I couldn't bend the tip and it just kind of stayed in that extended position from the start.

RESULTS: Physical Examination of Right Ring Finger shows:

**Inspection:** Right ring finger is extended, with visible swelling at the distal interphalangeal joint.

**Palpation:** Tenderness localized at the distal interphalangeal joint of the right ring finger.

**Range of Motion:** Patient unable to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint while attempting to make a fist. No joint laxity.

**Neurovascular Assessment:** Normal capillary refill, no sensory deficits.
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet finger (extensor tendon rupture at the distal interphalangeal joint)
